transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, yeah, nice to meet you too. Um, well, what really pushed me to finally make this appointment is... I just keep starting these follow-up items at work. I'm an auditor, so there's always a ton of follow-up after audits, or even after these mentorship events I run. I'll sit down with every intention of finishing them. I even bought this new planner—it's got these little color-coded stickers, which I thought would help because my sister uses them and swears by them. She's a teacher, so she's always organizing something. But anyway, I'll start the task, and then days later, I find out that the final email, or the review note, or the form never actually got done. It's just sitting there, half-finished. Like, last week I was supposed to send out this summary email, and I got distracted because my cat knocked over a plant, and by the time I cleaned up the dirt, I totally forgot what I was doing. So yeah, the follow-ups just aren't getting finished.
Did you have similar trouble finishing tasks or staying focused when you were a child?

Oh, absolutely. Even back in elementary school... I remember my report cards always said the exact same thing. They'd say I was bright, but I constantly lost my assignments, or I'd just rush past all the small details. And I talked out of turn a lot. Actually, my third-grade teacher, Mrs. Gable—she had this huge collection of ceramic frogs on her desk. Like, dozens of them. I always wondered where she bought them all, or if students just kept giving them to her as gifts, you know? Because what do you even buy a teacher? I usually just give Starbucks gift cards now. 

But anyway, she was always having to remind me to finish my classwork. My mother still jokes about it to this day. She always says I could completely ace a test, but then I'd totally forget the big project just sitting right there in my backpack. It was this bright pink Lisa Frank backpack, too, with the neon dolphins. God, I loved that thing. I took it everywhere until the zipper finally broke on a family trip to Florida...
Do you get unwanted thoughts that keep intruding into your mind and feel hard to dismiss?

Unwanted thoughts? Um, no, not really. I mean, my mind is always going a mile a minute, but it's not like I'm having bad thoughts I can't get rid of. It's more just... thinking about a million things at once. Like yesterday, I was trying to reconcile this account, and suddenly I was wondering if I ever paid my water bill, which reminded me that I need to buy a new filter for the Brita pitcher. I got the pitcher on sale at Target, actually. Target's dangerous for me, I always go in for one thing and come out with a cart full of stuff I don't need. Last time I bought this throw pillow shaped like a taco. It's hilarious, but it doesn't match my couch at all. My couch is this dark grey microfiber—super easy to clean, which is great because of the cat. But yeah, no, not like scary or weird thoughts that I can't shake. Just regular thoughts, but a lot of them.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about everyday things?

Worrying excessively? Um... I don't think so. I mean, I worry about normal stuff, I guess. Like getting my audits done on time, or if I remembered to lock the front door. Oh, actually, speaking of the front door, I just got this new smart lock installed last week. It's supposed to connect to my phone so I can check it from anywhere, which is super convenient, but the app keeps crashing. I spent like forty-five minutes on hold with customer service on Tuesday. The hold music was that one classical song—what is it, Vivaldi? Spring? Anyway, it was so loud and staticky. I ended up just hanging up because my cat started scratching at the screen door. He loves trying to get out onto the balcony, even though he's strictly an indoor cat. I bought him this elaborate cat tree to distract him, it's got three different levels and a little hammock... but yeah, I wouldn't say I worry excessively. Just normal worrying, really.
